notes: Building and Engineering News, vol. 15 part 2 (Internet Archive buildingengineer15215cont), the 26 weekly issues from 7 July to 29 December 1915. Same method as the later volumes: every numbered entry under Building Permit Applications and Building Contracts was taken from the djvu.xml OCR, East Bay headings set aside, and each San Francisco lot built from the block corner on the DPW street centrelines and compared with the sf-parcels shapes; a placement was accepted where the lot starts within two feet of a lot line of today (or the record names an unambiguous corner) and the roll dates the building 1914-1917, and alterations were matched by printed street number in sf-eas-addresses where the roll dates the building before 1915. The labels are printed with leader dots and each item is printed once. The OCR garbles many item numbers, so extract.py was run with BEN_LOOSE=1, which also takes an entry under a type heading whose number it cannot read; the item numbers of the published rows were then read from the page image, and unresolved rows whose number was not read carry no extra.item and say so in the locator. Every published row was read against the page image, location first, and its raw text was written from the image; a cost or name that could not be read on the image was left out (the totals at 151 21st Avenue, 207 Banks Street, 370 Ellis Street, 2060 Mission Street, 445 Sutter Street and 518 25th Avenue run into the next column or leaf). Descriptions of rows marked confidence low were built from the OCR and have not been read against the image. Owners are private individuals and are cut everywhere (raw.note; scrub_owner.py removes the fragments the OCR garbles past the first cut); a firm or institution named as owner is kept, and where the contractor, architect or designer named is the owner, shares the owner's surname or is listed at the owner's own address or beside the building site that name is cut too, with the owner firm. Sub-trade contracts are timeline entries and set no builder credit. Completion notices (printed in this volume as dated lines without item numbers), liens, sub-contracts printed 'on above' and the news columns were not taken. The paper came out on Wednesdays; issue dates are set from the mastheads (issues.json beside the corpus: first leaf of each issue, four leaves before the masthead that prints 'San Francisco' and the date). Seven single houses that were read against the image and have no architect or no name left to publish sit with the held single houses. Two held facts whose parcels got a page from this volume were read and published: a February 1916 contract to complete the flats at 36 Ashbury Street after a wind storm, and 1927 fire repairs at 233 Post Street.

coverage.remaining: Vols. 15 pt. 2 to 31 read (July 1915 to January 1932); the first half-year volume of 1915 is unread, buildingengineer1515cont. In this volume: 130 rows placed on a parcel whose roll year fits, single houses with no architect named and no page, are logged and held until another fact gives the parcel a page (extra.placed_apn; all but seven still need the image check). 276 rows have a nearest parcel that was not accepted (the lot starts off today's lot lines, or the roll dates the building outside the window). 576 rows were not placed: location lines not parsed (tract lots, garbled headings), street pairs that do not cross under the names read, and printed street numbers with no EAS row today.
coverage.note: 1,923 numbered entries read, 1,110 San Francisco rows, 534 placed on a parcel, 135 picked and read against the page image, 100 published on 96 pages (44 seeded), 28 held back: 23 storeys, unit counts or uses that contradict the roll, three pieces of minor work, one contract printed in the same issue as its permit and one misread street; seven more joined the held houses.
